characterActions.name: wave
characterActions.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Edit target/reference: attached character PNG, exact character identity and pixel style. Asset type: four-frame animation sprite sheet for this character. Output one square transparent PNG with a strict 2 by 2 grid of equal square cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. No grid lines, no labels, no borders. EACH cell contains ONE full-body version of the same character, at exactly the same scale. Center horizontally in each cell. Character height is 84% of each cell; standing foot baseline at 94% of cell height; head top at 10%. Original neutral proportions: large dark messy hair, friendly brown eyes and smile, white shirt with small gray emblem, black backpack straps, gray trousers, white shoes. Preserve outfit, face identity, palette, pixel block size; crisp pixels, no smoothing. Character does not change height/size between frames. Keep all motions small, within each cell. Background is truly transparent, no shadow or extra objects. Never mix neighboring cells. Motion brief: A friendly hand wave ONLY using the arm on the viewer's right. Frame 1: arm resting. Frame 2: forearm lifting halfway. Frame 3: open hand raised beside the head tilted outward. Frame 4: same raised forearm, hand tilted inward. Eyes and smile unchanged. Feet planted.

cursors.name: arrow
cursors.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: production retro desktop mouse cursor, a single transparent raster icon. Draw ONE classic northwest pointing arrow cursor, clean professionally drawn 1990s Macintosh / Windows pixel art. Pure white fill, continuous near-black one-pixel staircase outline, small gray lower-right inner shading. Familiar coherent arrow silhouette: sharp tip at upper left, long upright left edge, diagonal upper-right edge, two-pixel-wide angled stem joined cleanly below the arrow head. Work on a logical 32 by 32 square pixel grid, enlarge by exact nearest-neighbor to fill the output. Transparent background. Art fills a 26 by 29 region with tip at logical coordinate 2,2. No detached pixels, no holes, no fuzzy outlines, no antialiasing, no doodle, no illustration of a computer, no text, no shadow outside the outline. Legible as an actual small system cursor.

cursors.name: pointer
cursors.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: this transparent white glove cursor. Correct ONLY the hand gesture: keep the index finger extended pointing straight up, but fold the middle, ring, and little fingers DOWN into the palm, curled like a standard browser link-pointer cursor, with short knuckle bumps. Thumb sticks out to the left. The final silhouette must have ONE tall finger, NOT an open hand or raised middle finger. Keep the same white fill, near-black continuous pixel outline, gray lower-right inner shading, and retro pixel-art style. Reduce the long wrist to a short cuff. Actual transparent background. One isolated hand, no text, no scene, no antialiasing. Must read instantly as a classic system pointing-hand cursor at 32px.

cursors.name: wave
cursors.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: production retro desktop friendly character hover cursor, a single transparent raster icon. Draw ONE small welcoming open hand with four clearly separated raised fingers, thumb on left, rounded palm and short wrist. Same professional classic white glove cursor design as 1990s desktop UI, but warm peach fill to complement a sage-green and cream website. Near-black continuous one-pixel staircase outline, restrained deeper peach lower-right inner shading. Logical 32 by 32 square pixel grid enlarged by exact nearest-neighbor to fill output. Transparent background. Art occupies logical x3..29,y2..29, tallest middle fingertip at x16,y2. Connected natural hand anatomy, 5 fingers in total, no rings. No disconnected pixels, no holes, no fuzzy outlines, no antialiasing, no text, no external shadows or decorative sparkles. Legible and attractive at actual 32px cursor size.

refinementNotes: Regenerated the link hand with only the index finger extended.
Regenerated walking frame 3 to step with the opposite foot.
Aligned every frame to foot baseline y=184 and body center x=64 on a 128x192 canvas.
Normalized fixed-height gestures independently; retained the natural head dip for nod and tilt.
Used anticipation, brief peak holds and settling frames; returned to the original still pose after every gesture.
